formats.schema_description: XML. Root <InteractivePetrophysicsImagingTool> in namespace 'http://www.InteractivePetrophysics.com/ImageTool', preceded by an XML comment that documents units and enumerations. Root holds exactly ONE tool element whose NAME encodes the tool class: PadBasedTool(36) | LWDTool(12) | AcousticTool(10) | DipmeterTool(8) | CaliperTool(3) | MITTool(1) | Image360Tool(1) | Scan360Tool(1). Tool element carries attributes ID / Name / TemplateName / Company / Diameter(inches). Children are (a) scalar settings, (b) *Curve elements naming the LAS mnemonic that fills each role, (c) for pad tools a Stages > Stage > Arms > Arm > Pads > Pad tree. Pad is xsi:type ReferencedPad (points at an external .itp via ExternalPadID) or an inline DefinedPad. Geometry angles in degrees, offsets in inches.

XML. Root <AcousticWaveformToolDefinition>. TWO SCHEMA GENERATIONS SHIP SIDE BY SIDE: 23 files at the install root (older/flatter - ReceiverCurves/<string>, DistanceFromTransmitterToReceiver/<double>, has CoreMode + VerticalResolution + FrequencyVDL + FrequencySemblanceVDL, no RxTxOrientation) and 37 files under AcousticWaveforms\Tools\ (newer - DistanceFromTransmitterToReceivers/DistanceFromTransmitterToReceiver, TimeShifts/TimeShift, GainShifts/GainShift, adds RxTxOrientation, TheReceiverGroup, GainAction, TimeUnits, AnisoMethod, SembMethod, DispersionCorrectionValue, NptsToSmooth, PlotFileName*). Body = one <ToolTemplate> (tool-level identity + output curve lists + anisotropy/dispersion switches), N <ModeParameter> (per-mode SLOWNESS-PROCESSING defaults: filter band, slowness search, time window, semblance cutoff), and N matching <ModeSettings> (per-mode ACQUISITION geometry: receiver count, transmitter-to-receiver spacings, depth shift, sample rate, input curve wildcard mask). ModeParameter and ModeSettings are joined on ModeName.

XML. Root <Pad xsi:type="DefinedPad" ID=... Name=...> in the same ImageTool namespace, preceded by a comment stating that ButtonWidth / HorizontalOffset / HorizontalStep / VerticalOffset / VerticalStep are ALL IN INCHES and that ButtonRow/SourceCurve is an INDEX (e.g. [1]) into the SourceCurve list of the referencing tool's ReferencedPad. Body = ButtonCollections > N ButtonCollection (xsi:type=ButtonRow in 96/96 collections observed). A row is generated procedurally: Count buttons starting at (HorizontalOffset, VerticalOffset), each stepping by (HorizontalStep, VerticalStep), curve-sample index starting at StartIndex and advancing by IndexStep. Interlaced two-row pads are expressed as two ButtonRow collections with the same Count and a VerticalOffset difference.

Plain text, whitespace-delimited, NO fixed column widths. Lines beginning with '$' are free-text comments and carry the only documentation of sense-of-rotation and depth reference. Data lines are one row PER BUTTON, in the order the buttons appear in the source curve array. 17 of 18 files are 2-column: col1 = horizontal/circumferential offset, col2 = vertical(depth) offset. Weatherford OMI.bor is 1-column (horizontal offset only). Units are inches - stated in the '$' comments (e.g. 'spacing is 0.2 inch', 'depth reference at 3.48"'), never in a header keyword. Row count equals the button count declared for that pad in the companion .eli.

fields.note: absent in Weatherford OMI.bor which is 1-column

formats.schema_description: Plain text, three parts. (1) Line 1 = literal banner 'Electrical Image Parameter file' plus a free-form timestamp. (2) A '$'-commented two-line column legend followed by ONE ROW PER PAD/CURVE, 7 whitespace-delimited fields: Name(curve mnemonic) | NumberButtons | ButtonSpacing | OrientationToAzimuth | DepthShift | RotationShift | ButtonOrderFileName(.bor, optional). (3) A trailer of nine fixed '$'-keyed directives, each followed by its value line, present in 16/16 files IN THE SAME ORDER: Tool Resolution arround borehole [sic]; Default Output image curve name; Default Input Low High / Output Low high Low Values; Default Clip output to input low high value; Default Normalize image / normalization window; Default Hole size; Default Azimuth input curve; Default Correct azimuth for magnetic deviation / deviation value; Default top / bottom depths. '-' is the null/unset token. The .eli is the legacy predecessor of the .itt/.itp pair and is the format that references .bor files.

output slowness curves. Convention: DT + mode token. DTC=compressional, DTST/DTS=shear/Stoneley by mode, DTXX/DTYY/DTXY/DTYX = cross-dipole tensor components, DTFast/DTSlow = fast/slow shear, AnisoAngle/FastAzi = anisotropy azimuth.
derived/QC outputs. Convention: '_Smooth' suffix = smoothed twin of a primary; 'Aniso*Map' = anisotropy diagnostic rasters; VPVS = Vp/Vs ratio.

WILDCARD patterns, not literal mnemonics. '*' matches the receiver index; ';' separates alternative patterns tried in order; ',' (rare) lists explicit mnemonics. This is how IP binds an arbitrary vendor waveform array to a mode.
legacy per-pad array mnemonics. Convention: a pad token + index (PAD1..PAD6, P1BTN/P2BTN, FCA1..FCD4, OBRA/OBRB, XPAD1..XPAD6).

reuse_assessment.item: Tool-class taxonomy (PadBasedTool / LWDTool / AcousticTool / DipmeterTool / CaliperTool / MITTool / Image360Tool / Scan360Tool)
reuse_assessment.form: Model SandiBumi's borehole-image tool registry on this 8-class split. It is a genuinely good decomposition: the class determines which fields are even meaningful (pad tools need arms+pads, LWD tools need SectorOffset+ToolAlignment, acoustic tools need DelayValue+FluidSlowness). Copy the IDEA and the field-set-per-class, write our own class names and our own schema.
reuse_assessment.ip_risk: none - a taxonomy is not expression

reuse_assessment.item: Unit declarations carried in the comment headers (Diameter/offsets/ButtonWidth = inches; angles = degrees; DelayValue = Microseconds; FluidSlowness = MicrosecondsPerFoot; DepthOfInvestigation Units enum)
reuse_assessment.form: Make units EXPLICIT-PER-FIELD in SandiBumi's tool schema, exactly as IP does with the Units attribute on DepthOfInvestigationValue. IP's own inconsistency (units in a free-text comment for .bor, in an attribute for .itt) is the anti-pattern to avoid: always an attribute.

reuse_assessment.item: The ';'-separated priority-ordered alias list on every *Curve element
reuse_assessment.form: SandiBumi's alias catalogue should resolve a ROLE (hole-deviation angle, pad-1 azimuth, relative bearing, Z accelerometer...) to an ORDERED list of candidate mnemonics, not a single name. This is the single most directly transferable idea in the whole target.
reuse_assessment.ip_risk: none - the mechanism is a convention

reuse_assessment.item: The observed role->mnemonic mapping itself (DEVI/DEV/INC for deviation, HAZI/DAZ/AZI1 for hole azimuth, P1AZ/P1NO for pad-1 azimuth, RB for relative bearing, GR, CVEL/SPD/MSPD for cable speed, AX/AY/AZ + FX/FY/FZ for accelerometer/magnetometer triads)
reuse_assessment.verdict: ADOPT AS EVIDENCE, RE-DERIVE THE CATALOGUE
reuse_assessment.form: These mnemonics are INDUSTRY names (they originate with the service companies, not with PGL). Use this target as EVIDENCE that a mnemonic is real and what role it fills, then cross-check each one against the Techlog family/alias catalogs and the IP2025 register already ingested, and enter it in SandiBumi's own catalogue with that cross-source citation. Do NOT bulk-import IP's lists as a file.
reuse_assessment.ip_risk: low - individual mnemonics are industry facts; the curated LIST as a compiled work is not ours

reuse_assessment.verdict: ADOPT THE PARAMETER SET, RE-DERIVE THE VALUES
reuse_assessment.form: The parameter set is the correct decomposition of an STC (slowness-time-coherence) job and SandiBumi should expose the same knobs. The universal values (MinSlow 40, SlowStep 2, Units us/ft) are defensible as an initial UI default WITH THIS FILE CITED. The per-tool values (TR spacings, DepthShift, SampleRate) are vendor tool geometry and must come from the tool's own datasheet, not from here.
reuse_assessment.ip_risk: low for the parameter set; the per-tool geometry table is vendor data - do not redistribute

reuse_assessment.item: Per-tool button geometry (.itp ButtonRow offsets, .bor coordinate tables, .eli pad tables)
reuse_assessment.form: This is the vendor's measured tool geometry, compiled by PGL, shipped under EULA. SandiBumi must let a USER import or enter their own tool geometry, and should ship at most a GENERIC parametric pad (count / spacing / row offset) that a user populates. Record here that the procedural ButtonRow encoding (Count + Offset + Step + StartIndex + IndexStep) is an elegant way to express an interlaced two-row pad in 2 lines - adopt THAT encoding, empty.
reuse_assessment.ip_risk: HIGH - this is the redistributable-data core of the target

reuse_assessment.item: The ButtonRow procedural encoding and the SourceCurve '[n]' indirection
reuse_assessment.form: Expressing a pad as (Count, ButtonWidth, StartIndex, IndexStep, H/V Offset, H/V Step) rather than an explicit coordinate list, plus an index reference into the parent tool's curve list, makes a pad definition ~2 lines and lets one pad file serve many tools. Worth copying as a design decision for SandiBumi's own pad schema.

reuse_assessment.item: The 'is this already corrected?' boolean family (ButtonsAligned / PadsAligned / SpeedCorrected / SwingArmCorrected / MagneticDeclinationApplied / CenterReProjectionNotRequired / StagesAligned / NavigationAligned)
reuse_assessment.form: This is a provenance contract: the tool definition declares WHICH corrections the incoming data has ALREADY had applied, so the software does not double-correct. Double-applying a speed correction or a pad-offset alignment is exactly the silent-wrongness failure SandiBumi's data-integrity discipline exists to prevent. Adopt this flag family into SandiBumi's image ingest contract.

reuse_assessment.verdict: ADOPT AS A WARNING, NOT A PATTERN
reuse_assessment.form: IP2018 ships 23 old-schema and 37 new-schema .att files in different directories with the same extension and the same root element, differing in element names and in the MEANING of SemblanceCutoff. SandiBumi should version its tool-definition schema explicitly (a schemaVersion attribute) and refuse to load an unversioned file.

tierC_flags.finding: NO Tier-C functionality is referenced by any of the 224 files in this target.
tierC_flags.evidence: Case-insensitive grep across all .itt/.att/.itp/.bor/.eli for 'entropy', 'SonicSaturation', 'Domain Transfer', 'Experienced Eye', 'neural', 'patent', 'proprietary' returned ZERO hits.

tierC_flags.finding: Entropy-based borehole-image speed correction (registered Tier-C) is NOT named here, but the schema reserves a slot adjacent to it.
tierC_flags.evidence: The .itt comment header states verbatim: 'SpeedCorrected - when true implies that data for this tool has already been speed corrected.' The <SpeedCorrected> ELEMENT is documented in 15+25+3+4 = 47 comment headers but is SET IN ZERO SHIPPED FILES (grep '<SpeedCorrected>' over all 72 .itt returns nothing). Likewise <SwingArmCorrected>: documented, never set. So the speed-correction ALGORITHM lives in the binary, not in these files; only the already-corrected FLAG is part of the data contract.
tierC_flags.tier: Tier-A (the boolean flag/provenance contract) is free to adopt; the entropy speed-correction ALGORITHM remains Tier-C name-only and is not disclosed by this target.
tierC_flags.action: Adopt the flag, do not pursue the algorithm.

tierC_flags.finding: Anisotropy processing names an in-file method, but it is a published-literature method, not a PGL brand.
tierC_flags.evidence: AnisoMethod="Alford (Time)" in 36/37 newer .att files; SembMethod="Semblance" in 36/37. Alford rotation is standard published cross-dipole processing - Tier A/B, not Tier C.

gaps.gap: SemblanceCutoff is SHIPPED IN TWO INCOMPATIBLE SCALES and the file never declares which.
gaps.detail: Value '.25' or '0.25' appears in 198 mode blocks; value '25' appears in 56. Same attribute, same schema, 100x apart. The split correlates with schema generation (newer AcousticWaveforms\Tools\ files mostly '.25'; older root files mostly '25') but is NOT clean - Tools\CLSS.att, Tools\Esonic.att, Tools\FWS.att use '25' while root\Generic.att and root\XMAC.att use '.25', and Tools\Scope.att contains BOTH in one file.
gaps.impact: SandiBumi must NOT adopt a numeric semblance-cutoff default from this source without deciding the scale itself. Adopting '25' as a fraction would disable the cutoff; adopting '.25' as a percent would reject almost everything.
gaps.resolution: not resolvable from these files - needs the IP manual or a run-time test

gaps.gap: FilterLow / FilterHigh carry NO unit anywhere in the file.
gaps.detail: Values run 1 to 30 (FilterLow) and 3 to 30 (FilterHigh). The ToolTemplate declares TimeUnits for the time axis but there is no FrequencyUnits attribute anywhere in the schema.
gaps.impact: kHz is the only physically sensible reading for a sonic bandpass at these magnitudes, but that is INFERENCE, not a file statement. Recorded as inference, not as fact.

gaps.gap: .bor files carry no machine-readable tool identity.
gaps.detail: Tool name, pad numbers, sense of rotation and depth reference exist ONLY in free-text '$' comments (e.g. 'Button order for Baker STAR tool pads 1, 3 and 5' / '24 buttons order is anti-clockwise around hole. Button 2 is the depth reference at 3.48"'). Two files (HAL_EMIpads_1_3_5.bor, HAL_EMIpads_2_4_6.bor) even misspell the vendor as 'Halliburtom'.
gaps.impact: Any importer must treat the .bor comment block as documentation for a human, not as metadata.

gaps.gap: .eli column units are never declared in the .eli itself.
gaps.detail: The two-line '$' legend names the columns (Number Buttons / Button Spacing / Orientation to Azimuth / Depth Shift / Rotation Shift) but states no units. Inches for spacing and degrees for orientation are corroborated only by the companion .bor comments and by the equivalent .itt/.itp fields which DO declare units.
gaps.impact: Cross-format corroboration is required; do not read a .eli standalone.
gaps.resolution: corroborated via .itp comment header (inches) and .itt comment header (degrees)

gaps.gap: Data-entry defects exist in the shipped set - the vendor's own data is not clean.
gaps.detail: Baker WGI.itt has <ZAccelerationCurve>sec</ZAccelerationCurve> - 'sec' is a unit string in a field that must hold a curve mnemonic. Two .itt files (Schlumberger Dual OBMI, Lower.itt and Schlumberger Dual OBMI, Upper.itt) share the SAME ID 'Schlumberger Lower OBMI v1.1' despite being different tools. Weatherford HMI Lower.itp / Upper.itp declare ID/Name 'Standard HMI Lower/Upper v1.0' - no vendor prefix, unlike every sibling.
gaps.impact: Confirms the rule: do not treat vendor reference data as authoritative without validation. SandiBumi's importer needs a uniqueness check on tool ID and a mnemonic-shape check.
gaps.resolution: flagged; these are defects in the source, not parse errors

gaps.gap: Vendor naming is inconsistent BETWEEN formats.
gaps.detail: .itt Company uses full names (Schlumberger 26, Halliburton 13, Baker 11, Weatherford 10, Pathfinder 2, GOWell 1, empty 9). .att Company uses abbreviations (SLB 9, WFT 8, HAL 7, BHI 6, GE 2, Pathfinder 2, Gowell 2, APS 1, empty 23). 'Baker' vs 'BHI' and 'GOWell' vs 'Gowell' are the same vendor spelled differently in the same install.
gaps.impact: A vendor lookup keyed on this string breaks across formats. SandiBumi needs a canonical vendor id with an alias table - the same discipline as the mnemonic alias catalogue.
gaps.resolution: resolved by observation; SandiBumi should canonicalise

gaps.detail: Binary; excluded from this target by instruction. Their content and relationship to the text formats is unknown and is NOT inferred here.
gaps.impact: The catalogue may be incomplete with respect to whatever .t83 holds.

gaps.gap: DepthOfInvestigationValue is EMPTY in 17 of 72 .itt files.
gaps.detail: 10 files declare Units='Feet' with an empty value, 7 declare Units='Inches' with an empty value. DepthOfInvestigationCurve is present in 68/72 files and EMPTY in all 68.
gaps.impact: Depth of investigation is genuinely absent for those tools - recorded as 'not present in file', not filled with a textbook value.
